title: Use of N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) contaminated valsartan products and risk of cancer: Danish nationwide cohort study
authors: Pottegård A, Kristensen KB, Ernst MT, Johansen NB, Quartarolo P, Hallas J
followUp: median 4.6 years, to 30 June 2018, with a one-year lag
population: Danish patients aged 40 years or older without previous cancer using valsartan in 2012 to 2017
funder: Funding: None. The authors declare no support from any organisation for the submitted work.
authorConflicts: No financial relationships with any organisations that might have an interest in the submitted work in the previous three years.
result: 3625 participants contributed 7344 person-years unexposed and 3450 contributed 11,920 person-years ever exposed to NDMA. 104 cancers among unexposed and 198 among exposed: adjusted hazard ratio for overall cancer 1.09 (95% CI 0.85 to 1.41), without dose-response (P=0.70); colorectal cancer 1.46 (0.79 to 2.73), uterine cancer 1.81 (0.55 to 5.90). The authors state that uncertainty persists about single cancers and that longer follow-up is needed.
